questions.prompt: In the bootlocalopus grader, explain why the trust boundary is the parent process rather than the worker, and what 'fixed' had to mean as a result.

keyPoints.text: The first reviewer's fixes were all correct, yet whether the private channel was even used honestly is itself decided inside the worker.
keyPoints.quote: including whether the private channel was used honestly

keyPoints.text: Making the worker trustworthy against arbitrary code is a losing game.
keyPoints.quote: which is a losing game against arbitrary code

keyPoints.text: So the worker is treated as a source of untrusted data and the parent is the boundary.
keyPoints.quote: the worker is treated as a source of untrusted data

keyPoints.text: Faking a pass would mean fabricating every per-test row one by one, in the shape the spec registered, because the worker sends the plan of test names before running any.
keyPoints.quote: rows are per-test facts the learner would have to fabricate one by one

keyPoints.text: The parent derives ok itself: non-empty, every row passed, no run-level error.
keyPoints.quote: non-empty, every row passed, no run-level error

keyPoints.text: The design depends on the parent being sceptical, not the worker being honest.
keyPoints.quote: The design does not depend on the worker being honest; it depends on the parent being sceptical.

questions.prompt: Walk through the three v1 grade forgeries and the specific mechanism that now neutralises each one.

keyPoints.text: Replacing globalThis.expect made every assertion a no-op; harness globals are now non-writable and non-configurable before learner code loads.
keyPoints.quote: The harness globals are defined non-writable and non-configurable

keyPoints.text: Forgery two imported parentPort from node:worker_threads and posted an ok: true verdict with a fake passing test row.
The port is copied into a module-scope constant and deleted from workerData before learner code loads.
keyPoints.quote: deletes it from `workerData`** before any learner module loads

keyPoints.text: Learner code posting on parentPort talks to nobody.
keyPoints.quote: Learner code that posts on `parentPort` is talking to nobody.

keyPoints.text: Patching Array.prototype.every; the trusted core's builtins are captured into locals at module evaluation.
keyPoints.quote: is captured into locals at module evaluation, before learner code exists

keyPoints.text: A patched prototype afterwards changes nothing the core does.
keyPoints.quote: A patched prototype afterwards changes nothing the core does.

questions.prompt: Beyond the forgeries, what other escapes did the review find, how were they closed, and what is the general lesson for any system that runs someone else's code?

keyPoints.text: The worker inherited the server's tsx loader and could import reference solutions; execArgv is now empty so .ts curriculum files are unimportable.
keyPoints.quote: the worker is a bare Node, no `tsx` loader, so `.ts` curriculum files are unimportable

keyPoints.text: An import policy denies worker_threads, vm, child_process, module and file URLs outside the run directory.
process.exit, kill, abort and similar are replaced with throwing stubs, and exiting is answered as a failure immediately.
keyPoints.quote: Exiting is answered as a failure immediately rather than at the timeout.

keyPoints.text: The worker also shared the server's PID, so process.kill(process.pid) from learner code took the whole server down.
keyPoints.quote: the worker shared the server's PID, so `process.kill(process.pid)` took the server down

keyPoints.text: Make the trusted side derive conclusions from evidence it can check.
keyPoints.quote: make the trusted side derive its conclusions from evidence it can check

keyPoints.text: And make the untrusted side unable to reach the trusted side's inputs.
keyPoints.quote: to make the untrusted side unable to *reach* the trusted side's inputs
